payload.rationale: I assign a 25% chance to the precise contract event: NASA GISS’s reported unsmoothed annual Land–Ocean Temperature Index for 2026 must strictly exceed both 1.28°C and its 2025 value. Equality with either threshold is insufficient. Background knowledge indicates that continued human-caused warming makes new records increasingly plausible, but annual variability—especially ENSO—can outweigh the warming trend over a single year. The 1.28°C threshold represents exceptional recent warmth on the GISS baseline, rather than an ordinary year along the trend. With no supplied 2025 annual value or 2026 observations, this is a broad judgment, not a forecast conditioned on temperatures already observed through September. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that unfavorable ENSO conditions could keep 2026 below 1.28°C; an even higher 2025 value would also raise the hurdle. The strongest reason it could be too low is that substantial warmth may already have accumulated during 2026, potentially reinforced by El Niño or persistent ocean warmth. Such observations could make a record much more likely than this information-poor estimate suggests.
limitations: No outside evidence records were supplied, and no browsing was available.
The 2025 GISS annual value, 2026 monthly temperatures, and current ENSO conditions are unavailable here.
The threshold applies specifically to NASA GISS’s baseline and reported annual index; other temperature datasets are not interchangeable.
Strict comparison, reporting precision, and any applicable source revisions can matter near the thresholds.
